title: Microsoft Purview: time-limited role group assignments
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents optional assignment expiry, its limits, exclusions and audit behaviour, and the roadmap facts match. Minor corrections should clarify the expiry route, the underlying licensing requirement and differences between Microsoft's role documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-01T23:00:07.
The roadmap describes a limit in days for temporary admin permission when assigning users and security groups to role groups.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview is introducing the ability to set a limit in days when assigning users and security groups to role groups. This allows admins to define a fixed duration when providing admin permission on a temporary basis.

claims.claim: Individual and security-group assignments to the same role group retain independent expiration dates.
claims.quote: If a user receives the same role group through both an individual assignment and a security group assignment, each assignment retains its own expiration date.

claims.claim: The documented portal steps for managing role-group members and expiry require the Role management role.

claims.claim: Global administrators can manage role-group assignments and expiry.

claims.claim: The permissions page says Role Management is assigned only to Organization Management.

claims.where: Scope: Clouds and platform; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn restricts security-group role-group membership to Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organisations, unlike the broader roadmap cloud list.
claims.quote: Security groups are supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organizations.

claims.claim: PIM for Groups enables just-in-time user activation through security groups assigned to Purview role groups.
claims.quote: By using PIM for Groups, you can assign Microsoft Entra security groups to Microsoft Purview role groups in the Microsoft Purview portal. This assignment allows users to activate just-in-time access and then perform tasks in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Direct user assignments to Purview role groups cannot manage just-in-time activations.
claims.quote: you can't manage just-in-time activations by using direct user assignments to role groups in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Expiry is reached in the Purview portal through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users > user > Edit expiration.
claims.quote: On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups. ... Select Select. ... If the selected users or groups need temporary access, select the users or groups and select Edit expiration.
claims.fix: For the documented built-in-group route, use 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users > user > Select > user > Edit expiration'. Add to the note: 'For a custom group, continue through Name the role group and Edit roles of the role group to Edit members of the role group.' Both routes are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions#manage-role-groups; the current route omits intermediate wizard headings and the member-picker confirmation.

claims.claim: Choose groups follows the same documented expiry steps for security groups.
claims.quote: On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups. ... If the selected users or groups need temporary access, select the users or groups and select Edit expiration.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation for configuring this Purview role-group assignment expiry.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "role group" "expiration" "PowerShell"' and '"Purview" "role group" "expiration" "Graph"'; read purview-permissions, Add-RoleGroupMember and Update-RoleGroupMember. No expiry-setting operation found.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the PowerShell operation for searching these audit records.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Adding an expiration date is recorded in Microsoft Purview permissions audit logs.
claims.quote: The expiration date is recorded as part of the audit logs for Microsoft Purview permissions when the date is added or updated by the admin.

claims.claim: Updating an expiration date is recorded in Microsoft Purview permissions audit logs.

claims.claim: UpdatePermission is the searchable audit operation for editing a user assignment expiration date.
claims.quote: | Updated user role assignments expiration in role group | UpdatePermission | A user assignment expiration date is updated in an RBAC role group. |

claims.claim: Audit searching requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the role sentence in controls[1].note and its rendered copy with: 'Needs the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role in the Microsoft Purview portal for UI searches; audit cmdlets require one of those roles in the Exchange admin center and run in Exchange Online PowerShell.' The role names are correct but their separate assignment surfaces are not explained. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-search.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence, separate price or meter specific to temporary role-group assignment expiry is published in the examined Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview temporary role group assignments expiration licensing license service description'; read purview-permissions and the Purview service description; searched the latter for temporary, expiry and role groups. No feature-specific licence, price or meter found.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published a feature-specific licence.
claims.quote: Any user benefiting from the service requires a license. ... Users with a Purview role assigned for use in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' for this option within licensed Purview solutions. Replace licensing.notes with: 'Users with a Purview role assigned for use in the Microsoft Purview portal require the applicable Purview solution licence. Microsoft has not published a licence, separate price or meter specific to temporary role group assignment expiry at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. Retain the narrow feature-specific gap in the body rather than implying product licensing is wholly unpublished.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant-wide setting requiring expiry on these assignments.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview automatically expiring permissions require expiration tenant wide policy role groups'; read purview-permissions, including Temporary permissions and all Manage role groups steps. No tenant-wide requirement control found; expiry is optional per assignment.
